children: Odisha has approved technology projects worth about Rs 1.45 lakh crore, led by a proposed Rs 1.05 lakh crore integrated data centre.

The projects were cleared at the 46th meeting of the High-Level Clearance Authority (HLCA), chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi. The authority approved 27 projects with a combined proposed investment of Rs 2,47,115.70 crore across 15 districts, with the projects having the potential to create 50,162 jobs, according to the state government.

The IT, IT-enabled services and data-centre projects alone account for about Rs 1,42,941 crore. This segment formed the largest component of the latest investment pipeline. The addition of a Rs 2,078 crore semiconductor project takes the technology-related investment pipeline to roughly Rs 1.45 lakh crore.
High Density Datacentre Ltd has received clearance to establish an integrated data centre in Khurda with a proposed investment of Rs 1,04,550 crore and potential employment of 1,000 people.

HCLTech will invest Rs 14,257 crore in an AI-optimised data centre in Khurda, with potential employment of 385. HCLTech had earlier announced that the facility would be its first AI data centre and would be developed in partnership with Sarvam and the Odisha government as part of the state's planned sovereign AI ecosystem.
In Puri, Sentraforge AI Ltd has received approval for an AI data centre and global capability centre involving a proposed investment of Rs 22,634 crore and potential employment of 2,320 people.
RKD Construction Private Ltd will establish another data centre in Cuttack with an investment proposal of Rs 1,500 crore and potential employment of 220.
The semiconductor component of the approvals includes SiCSem's proposed Rs 2,078 crore facility in Khurda to manufacture silicon carbide wafers and gallium nitride products.

The SiCSem approval comes as Odisha seeks to establish itself as a semiconductor manufacturing hub. The state recently said it had received Rs 23,600 crore of semiconductor-related investment proposals and was developing an Odisha Silicon Valley across 870 acres at Naraj near Cuttack.

The latest HLCA approvals extend beyond digital infrastructure. Power and renewable energy projects account for Rs 54,287.70 crore, including a proposed 3,200 MW thermal power plant by NLC India in Deogarh and a 1,080 MW plant in Angul.
Steel, lab-grown diamonds, green energy, healthcare, chemicals, textiles, shipbuilding and advanced manufacturing are among the other sectors represented in the approvals.
